input.question: What is the reason for morning sickness and other"symptoms" in pregnant women? What, if any, are the advantages to us as a species?
input.ground_truth: (Biologist) Pregnancy sickness prevents the mother ingesting harmful toxins that could damage the embryo. As the embryo is developing (internal organs, limbs etc.) it is incredibly sensitive to toxins that would usually have no effect, e.g. asparagus is fatal to hamster embryos but is a perfectly suitable food for adults. Pregnancy sickness causes retching when these toxins (usually bitter tasting) are detected. It is incredibly useful: women who experience pregnancy sickness (about 75%) are half as likely to have a miscarriage than women who don't.

Question: What is the reason for morning sickness and other"symptoms" in pregnant women? What, if any, are the advantages to us as a species?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a tiny seed inside your tummy, and that seed is growing into a little baby. When that happens, your body gets a little confused and sends out some signals that make you feel sick in the morning, like wanting to throw up or feeling tired. This is called "morning sickness."

The reason this happens is because your body is changing a lot to help the baby grow. Sometimes, it gets a little mixed up and thinks there’s something yucky inside, so it tries to get rid of it by making you feel sick.

But here’s the good part: scientists think that this might help keep the baby safe! If there are any germs or things that could hurt the baby, sometimes morning sickness might help the body get rid of them. It’s like your body’s way of trying to protect the baby while it’s growing.

So, even though it feels icky, morning sickness might have helped people have healthier babies for a very long time. That’s why we still have it today!
